props.title: House of the Seven Gables

sections.content: Vincent Price delivers one of his earliest gothic performances in this atmospheric Universal Studios adaptation of Nathaniel Hawthorne's novel. House of the Seven Gables (1940) established many haunted house tropes that would influence later films like The Haunting (1963) and The Innocents (1961). Director Joe May, a German expressionist emigre, brings moody lighting and psychological tension that elevates this beyond typical Universal horror fare of the era. The film's exploration of ancestral curses and family sins would later echo in works like The Fall of the House of Usher (1960) and Crimson Peak (2015).

sections.content: The film's New England gothic atmosphere draws from the same well as The Devil and Daniel Webster (1941) and I Married a Witch (1942), mixing American historical settings with supernatural elements. The cursed house itself becomes a character, with cinematographer Milton Krasner's shadows and angles making the mansion feel alive with malevolent intent. This architectural menace would influence later haunted house films from The Haunting of Hill House (1999) to Crimson Peak (2015).

Price's performance as Gerald Pyncheon shows his early dramatic range before becoming horror's elegant villain in films like House of Usher (1960) and The Pit and the Pendulum (1961). The supporting cast, including George Sanders and Margaret Lindsay, brings gravitas to the period drama elements while maintaining the underlying supernatural tension that would become a hallmark of Price's later work. movies.title: Fall of the House of Usher
movies.slug: Roger Corman and Vincent Price adapt Poe's classic tale of family madness

sections.content: The film represents Hollywood's growing sophistication with literary horror adaptations in the 1940s, alongside works like Jane Eyre (1943) and The Uninvited (1944). These films established a more psychological approach to horror that would influence the genre for decades, seen in later works like The Others (2001) and The Woman in Black (2012).
